items.title: 67259_Big Chief Moore oral history interview
items.q: I didn't know who Louis Armstrong was... I finally got nerve enough to ask one of the listeners outside... I saw the picture... under there was the name, Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Very beautiful. That's -- I'm sure that a song like that and a -- and a kind of a melody and the flavor that that melody has has appeared in some of your work as you became a professional musician. Would you feel -- do you feel that some of that a, that feeling and that melody has come up in things that you've played over the years in various orchestras when you've been playing with people like Buster Bailey and Henry "Red" Allen?

Oh yes, yes, yes, yes. I learned the art of projection -- to project to the listeners in the audience by watching the great musicians that I have worked with. As you say Buster Bailey and "Red" Allen and Louis Armstrong and many, many greats that I can't a -- I could mention, I mean in the short space of time like we -- like here. I have worked with many. I've learned how to, how to get that rhythm and also the blues and sing things like "Basin Street", "Saint James Infirmary". And some on my albums are -- are on…

you learn a few things from somebody that is unknown. You'd be surprised how many I've listened to that I have never heard name mentioned before, and you know who they are. I go to a club; I listen, and I get things like that.

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: he had Lips Page on trumpet, Big Chief on trombone, and, well, you probably want to know all the musicians that, but the next little combo that Bechet had.

ctx.x: It's amazing, I think, for us, especially those of us who have not traveled extensively, it's hard for us to realize that jazz has made this tremendous inroad. And it's gone into every country.

It's, listen, man, it's something that nobody can change. I'll tell you why. when Bechet was in Paris playing at a jazz festival one time, Charlie Parker was living there and he was on that bill. So they're going to give Paris something new. But they still got the good old timers there in case something go wrong and good thing they had him. Charlie Parker wouldn't even speak to Bechet coming up or going over on the plane because he's, you know, just going to be here. But Bechet ain't worried about him because he…
What about some of the, some of the far out musicians, Louie? Are they saying anything with their music? Are they, are they really talking?
